subject: Variable rebate 'Swingline' exhibit — redline and fallback math
messages:
From: Simon Price <simon.price@acerohealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@acerohealth.com
Date: 2025-10-14T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit E - rebate mechanism (redline attached)

Nikhil,

Thanks for sending the draft order form last week. Our legal team attached an Exhibit E redline (Acero_Exhibit_E-Redline.pdf) with a couple of concerns around the "swingline"/variable rebate language and the interplay with caps/floors. High level: we need certainty that credits won't accumulate indefinitely and that the vendor (Redwood) can't claw back credits beyond a defined true-up window.

Two specific asks from our side:
- Can the swingline be explicitly capped as a percentage of committed monthly spend (we're proposing 15%)?
- We want an explicit expiry/forfeiture period for any smoothing credits (proposed 90 days after issuance).

We appreciate Redwood's flexibility; procurement wants to understand how this will affect quarterly accounting and whether the annual true-up would net the swingline. Attached is the redline. Can you confirm your legal/finance view on (a) a hard cap, (b) expiry window, and (c) sample amortization for the first six months?

Simon Price
Head of Procurement, AceroHealth
simon.price@acerohealth.com

--Attachment: Acero_Exhibit_E-Redline.pdf (pdf)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.inference>
To: Simon Price <simon.price@acerohealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.inference, laura_bennett@redwood.inference
Date: 2025-10-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit E - rebate mechanism (redline attached)

Simon — thanks, received. looping in Marissa (AM) and Laura (Legal) to confirm commercial/contract language. Quick thoughts from our side:

1) Cap: We can accept a hard cap; 15% of committed monthly spend is reasonable as a starting point, but would like to propose 20% as an alternative if Acero is open to a 12-month minimum consumption commitment.

2) Expiry: We agree credits should not be perpetual. Our standard is a 90-day expiration window from issuance, reconciled at an annual true-up. We can include language that makes credits non-cumulative across fiscal years.

3) Reconciliation mechanics: suggest the following language for Exhibit E (draft in redline-comparison.xlsx):
   - "Swingline Credits" defined as temporary usage smoothing applied to monthly invoices up to X% of committed monthly spend; credits expire after 90 days and are reconciled at the annual true-up.
   - True-up is performed within 60 days following the end of Redwood's fiscal year; any net owed amounts are invoiced, and any net credits beyond the 90-day expiry are forfeited.

Example math (illustrative):
   - Committed monthly spend: $200,000.
   - 15% swingline cap = $30,000 per month available as smoothing credit.
   - If Acero underutilizes in Q1 by $45k total, $30k (month 1 cap) + $15k (month 2) would be available, but all issued credits older than 90 days at the time of annual true-up will be forfeited.

I'm attaching a quick redline comparison (redline-comparison.xlsx) that shows the proposed language and an alternative that ties the cap to committed ARR rather than monthly spend. Laura — could you help propose precise contract wording to avoid ambiguous terms like 'may be applied'?

Next steps: Laura to produce final legal redline; Marissa will confirm if Sales is ok trading a higher swingline cap for a 12-month commit.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.inference

--Attachment: redline-comparison.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
To: Simon Price <simon.price@acerohealth.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.inference>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.inference, karthik_iyer@redwood.inference
Date: 2025-10-15T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Exhibit E - rebate mechanism (redline attached)

Simon / team — thanks for the redline. I've reviewed and proposed contract language in the attached order form draft (orderform-draft-v3.docx). Key legal clarifications we made:

- Remove ambiguous verbs: replace "may be applied" with explicit "will be applied to monthly invoices up to the swingline cap as defined below."
- Define expiration: "Swingline Credits shall expire 90 calendar days after issuance and are non-cumulative across fiscal years. Any credit that has expired shall be forfeited and shall not reduce Customer's payable amounts at annual true-up."
- Floor definition: replace free-form floor language with a formula: "Floor = max(Committed Monthly Spend * 0.80, Minimum Monthly Fee)."
- Non-recourse clause: "Redwood shall not seek repayment of issued Swingline Credits except to the extent of manifest error, fraud, or gross negligence."

Also propose administrative timing: true-up to be completed within 60 days of Redwood's fiscal year end with invoice adjustments due net 30.

If Acero accepts a 12-month minimum commitment the Sales team has agreed to waive the early-termination true-up penalty for the first quarter only, conditioned on mutually-agreed usage forecasts. That concession is reflected in the order form.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.inference

--Attachment: orderform-draft-v3.docx (docx)

Nikhil/Laura — appreciate the quick turn. Acero will accept the 15% hard cap and the 90-day expiry language as drafted; a couple of quick operational questions before we circulate for CFO sign-off:

1) DocuSign timeline: can Redwood turn the final order form around for signature within 5 business days of final agreement?
2) Amortization: can Redwood provide an illustrative 6-month amortization table for the swingline credits (we want to run this through our accounting). If Sales is offering the 20% cap in exchange for a 12-month commit, we need numbers for both 15% and 20% scenarios.

If those are OK, Procurement will schedule CFO review for next Tuesday.

Simon
